newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea Metals - Economic woes cap domestic demand.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea Metals - Economic woes cap domestic demand.

text.p: A sharp decline in aluminium prices has failed to lift South Korean metal demand this week which has been hit by domestic economic woes, traders said on Thursday.
Three-month London Metal Exchange (LME) aluminium was quoted at $1,560/62 a tonne early on Thursday morning in London against an eight-month high of $1,651 on January 24.
Domestic aluminium prices have fallen to about 1.50 million won a tonne from 1.51 million won a week ago, while local copper prices were unchanged at around 2.279 million won a tonne.
But South Korean aluminium import premiums for spot delivery have remained flat at $90 a tonne CIF Pusan over LME cash prices, traders said.
Zinc and lead prices were unchanged at 1.079 million won and 728,000 won a tonne respectively.

The drop in aluminium prices has been partially offset by the won's decline against the dollar as the currency's fall has further dampened local buyers' interest already withered by the financial troubles of insolvent Hanbo Steel Co, they said.
"Most metal importers are incurring heavy losses due to the local currency's steep decline against the dollar," a metal analyst with Daewoo Economic Reseach Institute told Reuters.
Many companies are still having difficulties in getting loans from local banks after the Hanbo crisis due to their tougher credit screening, the analyst said.
Two bankers and lawmakers have been arrested in connection with the loans to Hanbo Steel, which racked up a total of five trillion won in loans before insolvency in late January.
The won had plunged 3.6 percent to 874.40 on Thursday from 844.50 on January 3, pressured by the Japanese yen's weakenss against the dollar and the country's rising trade deficit.
South Korea posted a record monthly trade deficit of $3.48 billion for January, compared with $2.13 billion a year ago.
